description: We are an interdisciplinary team building next-generation health care software designed to monitor, diagnose, and safeguard astronaut well-being during long-duration space missions. By bridging advanced telemetry with intuitive clinical tools, our platform ensures that crews stay healthy, resilient, and mission-ready millions of miles away from Earth.
summary:
**ASTRAHEALTH – AI-Powered Astronaut Health Monitoring and Early-Warning System**

ASTRAHEALTH, developed by Team BITCOSMOS, is an intelligent health monitoring software concept designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It aims to monitor important health indicators such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, sleep patterns, fatigue, stress levels and radiation exposure.

The system uses data analysis and AI-based anomaly detection to identify unusual changes in an astronaut's health readings and generate early-warning alerts. It provides a centralized dashboard with health trends, risk indicators and suggested actions for astronauts and mission-control teams. An important feature is its offline-first approach, allowing essential monitoring and alerts to function even during communication interruptions.

ASTRAHEALTH addresses the challenge of maintaining astronaut health in the demanding environment of space, where microgravity, radiation, isolation and communication delays create significant risks. By enabling continuous monitoring, personalized health assessment and timely alerts, the project aims to improve crew safety, support informed decisions and contribute to safer future Moon and Mars missions.
details:
ASTRAHEALTH: Monitoring Life Beyond Earth (Team BITCOSMOS)

What it does
ASTRAHEALTH is a prototype early-warning system for astronaut health on long-duration missions, where Earth-based medical help is delayed or unavailable. It monitors heart rate, SpO₂, temperature, respiratory rate and blood pressure, and compares each reading with that astronaut’s own baseline as well as with configured safety rules. It combines the two into a GREEN, AMBER or RED status, with the reasons and a suggested review action. Missing or unreliable sensor data raises a separate data-quality warning and is never treated as “normal.”

How it works
Each reading is validated, then checked by three layers: configured rule thresholds, statistical deviation from the astronaut’s personal baseline (including moving-average drift), and a multivariate anomaly score. A risk engine combines these, escalates repeated abnormal readings, and creates alerts with duplicate suppression. The system is designed offline-first: if communication is lost, monitoring continues locally, records queue in the browser’s IndexedDB, and they synchronise safely after reconnection using unique IDs so nothing is lost or duplicated.

Try it
The live demo runs in the browser with no installation. It has three fictional astronauts and four scenarios: normal health, gradual anomaly, high-priority alert, and an offline mission.

Benefits and intended impact
The aim is to give crews and mission control earlier, explainable warnings without constant ground contact. Personal baselines matter because population ranges may not suit every astronaut in microgravity. The system supports decision-making and does not diagnose.

Tools used
Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, scikit-learn (Isolation Forest), pandas, NumPy, SciPy and ReportLab for the backend core. JavaScript, HTML, CSS, IndexedDB and a service worker for the browser demo. Node.js for testing. We used Claude (an AI assistant by Anthropic) to help write and test the code.

What is creative
Offline-first monitoring, per-astronaut baselines, and treating missing data as a warning rather than as normal. The demo makes all of this visible in under two minutes.

Factors we considered

  • Microgravity, radiation, sleep and isolation as drivers of physiological change.
  • Limited onboard computing and interrupted communication.
  • Privacy and safety. All data is synthetic, thresholds are prototype values and not clinical limits, anomaly scores are not disease probabilities, and this is not a medical device.

Current status and limitations
All data is simulated. The browser demo runs its own JavaScript version of the logic. The Python backend and its tests are in the repository, but its API layer has not yet been run end to end. A full React frontend connected to the backend is planned.
